body:
**Maintainer ruling (2026-08-10, directed in session `session_01BPWqbmEFU8gJepBJTHESXd`): the `type: 'form'` contract means in-shell, and an internal submit lands on the record.**

1. `/forms/:name` in `mode="internal"` nests inside the console shell (keep the route — deep-linking survives; the missing chrome is the defect, not the navigation).
2. Internal-mode submit defaults to redirect-to-created-record; `thank-you` stays the default for the public `/f/:slug` path only.
3. `showcase_task.edit` may declare a `submitBehavior` as an interim corpus fix, but the platform default is the ruling above — the corpus must not have to opt out of a wrong default.

The renderer changes land in objectui (`App.tsx` route nesting, `FormPage` mode-aware default) — per the file-at-destination ruling (#7167), the objectui half migrates there with this ruling quoted; this card tracks the contract statement.

`needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`.

**State correction by the `domain:devx` seat (#6023): `pm:dispatched` → `pm:blocked`, assignee cleared.**

`Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/objectui#4109`

**Why the label was wrong.** The objectstack half of this card shipped in PR #7417 (merged 2026-08-10 12:15Z, first line `Part of #7245`, deliberately not `Fixes`, so the card correctly stayed open for the renderer half). The renderer half migrated to **objectui#4109** per the file-at-destination ruling (#7167) and is `pm:dispatched` **in that repo, under that repo's seat**.

So nothing has been in flight *in this lane* since 08-10. `pm:dispatched` here asserts "a dev in this lane is working it", which was not true, and it hid the card from the one query that should return it: the unlock sweep over open `pm:blocked` issues. Left as-is, the card would have gone quiet until someone happened to re-read it — the failure mode the state model calls out, where a card waits on something with no mechanism watching for the wait to end.

**Assignee cleared** because a blocked card is not claimed — selection skips it either way, and an assignee with no owner is the one state the shared-identity protocol cannot interpret.

## ⚠️ Known gap in this correction, recorded rather than papered over

The `Blocked-by:` line above is in **this comment, not the issue body**, and the unlock sweep greps the **body**. I did not add it to the body deliberately:

GitHub has no partial-body edit — an update is a whole-body PATCH — and the MCP read returns this body HTML-escaped (`type: 'form'`, blockquote markers as `>`). Writing back what the read returned risks re-escaping a body that is dense with quoted code and blockquotes. **This is the same hazard, on the same tooling, that the outgoing PM measured on #7276** and correctly declined to gamble on; I am not going to reach a different conclusion about the same mechanism on a card that is not urgent.

**What this costs:** when objectui#4109 merges, the sweep will surface this card by label but will not auto-resolve the `Blocked-by:` reference. **Whoever runs that sweep should treat this comment as the machine half** and re-verify the card's premise at the merged ref before returning it to the queue — a merge that closes the renderer half is exactly the merge most likely to change what remains here.

The clean fix is a browser-side body edit (no PATCH-from-snapshot risk), which is the same remedy #7276 is already waiting on the maintainer for. Not filing a third card for one shared tooling limitation — flagging it here and in the round report.
